question.text: A competing offer in an open offer must be made within what timeframe from the date of the Detailed Public Statement (DPS) of the first offer?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (SAST) Regulations, a competing offer must be made by public announcement within 15 working days of the Detailed Public Statement of the first open offer. The first and competing offers then run on aligned timelines. The Trap: "21 calendar days" and "30 calendar days" are distractors — SAST timelines are specified in working days. It is also incorrect to say the original acquirer may match the competing offer price within 15 working days; the workbook permits acquirers to revise the terms of an open offer (including price) upward up to 1 working day before the commencement of the tendering period. Note: The first acquirer and any competing acquirer can each revise their offer upwards (price and/or size) up to 1 working day before the tendering period opens, subject to the procedural disclosures prescribed by SEBI.
